kalshi.question: What states will redistrict before the 2026 Congressional elections? — Kansas
kalshi.rules:

Formally adopted and enacted into law by the appropriate legislative or redistricting authority; AND
Not enjoined, vacated, stayed, or struck down in full by any court with jurisdiction over congressional redistricting in Kansas as of the Expiration Date; AND
In effect for use in the first scheduled federal election after its adoption

polymarket.question: Will Nicolás Maduro be the leader of Venezuela end of 2026?
polymarket.rules:
This market will resolve to the individual who officially holds the position of the head of state of Venezuela on Dec 31, 2026 at 12 PM ET.

For the purposes of this market, "officially holds" refers to the individual that was formally appointed, confirmed (if confirmation is required), and sworn in as the head of state of Venezuela or otherwise confirmed by official government information as being the head of state of Venezuela. 

If the Venezuelan government does not clearly state who is the head of state, the market will resolve to the individual who is listed as the Head of State by the UN (see: https://www.un.org/dgacm/en/content/protocol/hshgnfa).  

In the event that more than one official head of state is listed by the Venezuelan  government, this market will resolve to the individual who is listed as having primary status. If no distinction is made, the market will resolve to the individual who first assumed the position. 

If no individual holds the position this market will resolve to “No Head of State”. 

The following do NOT constitute "officially holding" the role: nominated, announced, or designated as the head of state of Venezuela but appointment not yet effective; appointed with an effective date after Dec 31, 2026; previously served as the head of state of Venezuela but term has expired, resigned, or been terminated before Dec 31, 2026; serving as the head of state of Venezuela in a consultant, contractor, or unofficial capacity; named as successor or heir apparent to the head of state of Venezuela but not yet appointed; or holding a different role with oversight of the head of state of Venezuela but not the specified position itself.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the UN recognized government of Venezuela. If the Government of Venezuela does not clearly state who is the head of state, information from the UN and a consensus of credible reporting may be used. 

Note: this market is mutually exclusive.

llm_verdict.divergence: Measurement moment differs by two hours (Kalshi 10:00 AM ET vs Polymarket 12:00 PM ET on Dec 31, 2026), and Polymarket's explicit UN-protocol-list fallback could name a different head of state (e.g., acting president Delcy Rodríguez) than Kalshi's 'official government directories/Source Agency hierarchy' reading, which Kalshi has already clarified favors Maduro.
llm_verdict.reasoning: Both target the same entity (Nicolás Maduro), same office (head of state of Venezuela), same date (Dec 31, 2026), and share verbatim the exclusion list for what does not count as 'officially holding.' Polarity aligns: a Polymarket resolution to the Maduro outcome corresponds to Kalshi YES, and both are structured as mutually exclusive multi-strike markets over candidate officeholders. However, three concrete wedges exist. (1) Timing: Kalshi measures at 10:00 AM ET, Polymarket at 12:00 PM ET — a resignation, removal, or swearing-in of a successor inside that two-hour window on Dec 31 would settle them oppositely, and this is not idle given Maduro's reported detention in the U.S. and Rodríguez's acting role. (2) Source hierarchy: Polymarket explicitly falls back to the UN protocol Head-of-State list (and 'consensus of credible reporting') if the Venezuelan government does not clearly state who is head of state; Kalshi relies on 'official government directories, organizational charts, or equivalent authoritative sources' plus its own Source Agency hierarchy. In a contested-recognition scenario these can point to different individuals. (3) Criteria structure: Kalshi's three prongs are disjunctive and its third prong explicitly disqualifies acting/interim service, whereas Polymarket's definition is a single clause with no explicit acting-capacity carve-out and adds tie-break rules (primary status, first assumed) plus a 'No Head of State' outcome that Kalshi does not spell out. Kalshi's April 2026 clarification pins the current state to Maduro-YES/Rodríguez-NO, and Polymarket would most plausibly reach the same answer since the Venezuelan government clearly states Maduro is constitutional president — so under present facts they match. Absent a change, they pay together; the divergence risk is concentrated in the unstable tail scenarios and the two-hour timing gap.

warnings: one side names a year the other does not

kalshi.question: Will the United States recognize Reza Pahlavi as the leader of Iran in 2026? — Before 2027
kalshi.rules: If the United States recognizes Reza Pahlavi as the leader of Iran before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes. For purposes of this Contract, the United States recognizes Reza Pahlavi when the government of the United States takes official action acknowledging Reza Pahlavi specifically as the rightful or legitimate leader of Iran. Recognition must be explicit regarding Reza Pahlavi as an individual, not merely recognition of Iran as a state or recognition of whatever government happens to be in power.

polymarket.question: US recognizes Reza Pahlavi as leader of Iran in 2026?
polymarket.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Trump administration announces that the United States officially recognizes Reza Pahlavi as the "leader of Iran" by December 31, 2026, 11:59 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Roles that could qualify for "leader of Iran" status include, but are not limited to, "head of state," "prime minister," or other similar roles that give him primary executive authority in the territory of Iran.

A qualifying US statement must be direct and unqualified. Conditional, hypothetical, supportive, or implied statements do not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US government and Donald Trump, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

llm_verdict.divergence: Kalshi counts any official US government action recognizing Pahlavi as the 'rightful or legitimate leader' (which a government-in-exile/legitimacy declaration would satisfy), while Polymarket requires an unqualified Trump-administration announcement recognizing him in a role conferring 'primary executive authority in the territory of Iran' — a symbolic legitimacy recognition of an exile figure could pay YES on Kalshi and NO on Polymarket.
llm_verdict.reasoning: Same entity (Reza Pahlavi), same recognizing party (US), same polarity, and effectively the same deadline (Kalshi: before Jan 1 2027; Polymarket: Dec 31 2026 11:59 ET — a difference of only hours, immaterial in practice). Both require explicit, non-implied recognition of Pahlavi as an individual. The material gap is in the definition of 'leader': Polymarket enumerates roles giving primary executive authority within Iranian territory, which arguably excludes recognizing him as the legitimate leader of a government-in-exile or as the rightful (but not de facto governing) leader — precisely the scenario Kalshi's 'rightful or legitimate leader' language appears to capture. Secondarily, Kalshi accepts action by 'the government of the United States' broadly (e.g., a State Department or congressional act), whereas Polymarket keys on a Trump-administration announcement, though Polymarket's 'official information from the US government' fallback softens this. Both would resolve NO in the overwhelming majority of states of the world, but the single most plausible YES pathway (recognition of an exile leadership) is exactly where the texts could diverge, so I cannot certify full equivalence.

kalshi.question: What states will redistrict before the 2026 Congressional elections? — Louisiana
kalshi.rules:
If the Louisiana legislature has adopted new, qualifying congressional district maps after Issuance and before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes. These maps must be:
Formally adopted and enacted into law by the appropriate legislative or redistricting authority; AND
Not enjoined, vacated, stayed, or struck down in full by any court with jurisdiction over congressional redistricting in Louisiana as of the Expiration Date; AND
In effect for use in the first scheduled federal election after its adoption

For clarity:
Maps that are temporarily stayed pending appeal but later upheld will resolve to YES if they are ultimately in effect by the Expiration Date
Maps that are completely redrawn by a court or special master will resolve to NO
Maps that are withdrawn by the Legislature before implementation will resolve to NO
If no new maps are adopted by Nov 1, 2026, the market will resolve to NO

polymarket.question: Will Louisiana use a new congressional map for the 2026 United States midterm elections?
polymarket.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the listed US state uses a new congressional district map for the 2026 United States midterm elections. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

To qualify, after the 2024 United States congressional elections, the listed state must have adopted a new congressional district map that is:
- Formally adopted and enacted into law by the appropriate legislative or redistricting authority;
- Not enjoined, vacated or otherwise fully struck down prior to the 2026 United States Midterm elections; and
- In effect for use in the 2026 United States midterm elections.

Maps that are temporarily stayed pending appeal but later upheld will qualify if they are in effect for use in the 2026 United States midterm elections.

Maps that are completely redrawn by a court, special master, or legislature before implementation will not qualify, unless the redrawn map is itself a new map used in the 2026 United States midterm elections. 

If the 2026 United States midterm elections occur and no new qualifying map is in use, this market will resolve to “No”.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be official information from the listed state and a consensus of credible reporting.

llm_verdict.divergence: Court/special-master-drawn maps: Kalshi resolves NO for any map 'completely redrawn by a court or special master,' whereas Polymarket explicitly counts such a redrawn map as qualifying if it is itself the new map used in the 2026 elections — a highly live scenario in Louisiana given the Callais litigation.
llm_verdict.reasoning: Both ask whether Louisiana will have a new congressional map for 2026, and share much boilerplate, but several clauses can settle them oppositely. (1) Court-drawn maps: Kalshi states flatly that maps completely redrawn by a court or special master resolve NO; Polymarket carves out an exception saying a court/special-master/legislature redrawn map qualifies if that redrawn map is itself the new map used in 2026. If SCOTUS's Louisiana v. Callais ruling forces a court-imposed remedial map, Kalshi = NO, Polymarket = YES. (2) Adopting authority: Kalshi's operative sentence requires adoption by 'the Louisiana legislature'; Polymarket accepts any 'appropriate legislative or redistricting authority.' (3) Qualifying window start: Kalshi counts only maps adopted after market Issuance (an unspecified date, likely mid/late 2025); Polymarket counts any map adopted after the November 2024 congressional elections — a map enacted in, say, early 2025 could qualify on Polymarket but not Kalshi. (4) Timing: Kalshi requires adoption before Nov 1, 2026 with status assessed at a Nov 8 expiration; Polymarket keys off the map being in effect for the Nov 3, 2026 election, with settlement dated Nov 3 — an injunction landing between Nov 1 and Nov 8, or an adoption on Nov 1-2, could split them. Resolution source is loosely specified on Kalshi and 'official state info plus credible reporting' on Polymarket, so agreement there is unverified. Any one of these is enough to break the hedge.
